label: NEW PATTERNS

cover.headline: 4 conflict habits *worth a second look*
cover.sub: Many of us learned them long before we got married.

points.heading: Keeping score
points.body: A running tally of who did what turns every talk into a trial. Try dealing with one thing at a time.
points.panel: Raise today’s issue, and only today’s.

points.heading: Going silent to keep the peace
points.body: Quiet can feel safer, but what goes unsaid often comes out sideways later.
points.panel: “I need a little time, and then I do want to talk about it.”

points.heading: Arguing to win
points.body: If one of you wins, the marriage doesn’t. Aim to understand before you aim to be right.
points.panel: “Help me understand how you see it.”

points.heading: Bringing up the past
points.body: Old hurts matter. They get a fairer hearing in their own conversation than in the middle of this one.
points.panel: “Is this about now, or about then?”

resource.name: Relationship Rewrite Method
resource.covers: Tools for looking at conflict, distance, and communication differently.

caption:
Nobody sits us down and teaches us how to disagree. We pick it up along the way, and then we bring it into our own marriage.

The good part is that a habit can be noticed, and what you can notice, you can change. If you’d like more structure for that, there’s a resource at the link in bio with tools for looking at conflict, distance, and communication differently. It’s one option, not a promise.

Follow @spotseason for more small steps.
